request: Check this flight: did a control fault occur, when, and where on the aircraft?

result.headline: No actuator control fault seen; airspeed and yaw-rate read zero all flight after a sensor-health error at 0.2 s.
result.explanation: A sensor-health error was logged at t=0.2 s. Airspeed and yaw rate stay at exactly 0 throughout, so those sensors are likely invalid. The roll, throttle and altitude oscillation looks like a sustained banked circling turn rather than an actuator fault.

evidence.quote: t=0.2 s mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: A sensor-health error is logged at the start of the flight
Both signals are flat at exactly 0 while the aircraft moves at 20+ m/s and its heading changes continuously; the sensors or their data are invalid
Roll follows its setpoint, so the roll axis is not failing; the setpoint is clamped near 45 deg
Three channels never move, so they are saturated or unused; no response can be assessed for them

checked.check: Roll and pitch setpoint tracking across the flight
checked.result: Roll tracks its setpoint within a few degrees; pitch swings but is bounded.

checked.check: Yaw-rate signal and airspeed against vehicle motion
checked.result: Both are constant 0 while heading and velocity change, so the sensors are invalid.
ch[0] and ch[6] sit at 1500 us and ch[7] at 1930 us for the whole flight.

effects.why: The throttle cycles with the circling turn and the altitude changes, so it is likely a response to the manoeuvre rather than a fault.
The yaw setpoint is unwrapped and keeps growing as the aircraft circles, so it is not a divergence on its own.

next_action.action: Inspect airspeed and gyro sensor health and the logged ch[7] function
next_action.why: This separates a real sensor failure from missing logging, and shows whether the three constant channels are intended.
how: Check the sensor-health status flags and EKF/estimator status at boot
Verify the airspeed sensor and gyro raw data
Check the servo/motor mapping for ch[0], ch[6] and ch[7]
next_action.conditions: Bench power-up with the battery near the voltage seen in this flight; compare with a normal flight log.
next_action.baseline: A normal flight of the same airframe with non-zero airspeed and yaw rate.

outcomes.label: Airspeed and gyro invalid at boot
outcomes.means: The sensor fault is real and explains the flat signals.

outcomes.label: Sensors fine, logging missing
outcomes.means: The zero signals are a data-recording gap, not a fault.

unknowns: Whether airspeed and yaw rate are truly invalid or simply not logged
What the low-voltage warning was relative to
Whether the roll angle is a commanded circling manoeuvre

hypotheses.claim: A sensor-health fault left airspeed and yaw rate reading zero for the whole flight.
hypotheses.because: The sensor-health error at 0.2 s coincides with signals that are flat at exactly 0 despite clear motion.

hypotheses.claim: A control-surface actuator fault caused the oscillation.
hypotheses.because: Attitude follows its setpoint and the channels move plausibly; there is no divergence or saturation event.

hypotheses.claim: The constant channels ch[0], ch[6] and ch[7] are unused or saturated, or the signals are not logged.
hypotheses.because: They are constant for the whole flight, so the data cannot show whether they should move.

events.why: This is the only fault-like event, and it matches the flat sensor signals.
A warning at t=0.2 s with no visible effect on the flight data.
